# ux-writing

On-demand reference adapted from the vendored MIT UI/UX Kit. Project policy
and frontend-design govern scope and completion.

Use concise task language and existing terminology. Action labels name the
action/object; errors explain the problem and a usable next step. Preserve
factual copy and never invent claims or captions to fill space.
Keep labels accessible, avoid color/direction-only instructions, and follow
existing localization conventions. Destructive confirmation describes the
actual effect with proportionate friction. Omit redundant helper copy.
